$comment: Growth-halt budgets for large public root barrels (MC-7 / DZUPAGENT-CODE-L-05 + ARCH-LOW-01)
and per-file LOC ceilings for god-module-prone packages (MC-5 / DZUPAGENT-CODE-L-04).
Each budget is pinned at the CURRENT measured baseline so the gate is green today and
RED on any growth. New public API must land on a documented subpath export
(see config/public-api-allowlists.json subpaths) instead of widening the root barrel.
Metrics:
maxRootBarrelExplicitExports - named re-exports counted across `export { ... } from` blocks in src/index.ts
maxRootBarrelStarExports     - `export * from` statements in src/index.ts
maxRootBarrelSourceCount     - distinct modules re-exported from src/index.ts
maxRootIndexLines            - line count of src/index.ts
auxiliarySourceLineBudgets   - per-file line caps for specific non-index source modules re-exported by the barrel
maxFileLines                 - per-file LOC ceiling applied to every src/**/*.ts (excl. tests/.d.ts) in the package
fileLineAllowlist            - REMOVED by RF-03. It was an uncapped boolean exemption that skipped measurement entirely; the gate now REJECTS the key. Use fileLineDebtPins.
rootDebtPin                  - exact source hash/commit/review-bound temporary ceiling above a root target
fileLineDebtPins             - exact source hash/commit/review-bound temporary ceilings for oversized files
shrinkTarget/shrinkTargets   - the budget a debt pin is expected to come back down to; the pin is temporary, the target is the real limit
Removing or renaming a root export is a published-consumer breakage and is NOT how you lower these numbers;
lower them only by relocating a cluster to a subpath while keeping a root re-export, which leaves counts flat.
Lower maxFileLines debt by extracting cohesive sub-modules, then deleting the file's fileLineDebtPins entry.
2026-08-18 RF-03 (DZUPAGENT-ARCH-H-07 + DZUPAGENT-CODE-H-06, audit full-dzupagent-2026-08-12/run-001):
fileLineAllowlist is GONE. It was an uncapped boolean exemption — check-barrel-budgets.mjs skipped
measurement entirely for a listed path, so a pinned file could grow without bound and the gate stayed
green. Measured drift under it: runtime-contracts/src/ai-execution.ts 0 -> 2496 LOC, memory/src/
observational-memory.ts 990, agent-adapters/src/model-discovery.ts 1349, agent/src/orchestration/
delegating-supervisor.ts 841 -> 979. All 21 live allowlist entries were converted to fileLineDebtPins,
which bind the accepted line count to the file's exact bytes (sha256), a source commit, a rationale and a
finite reviewBy — so ANY later edit to a pinned file fails the gate closed instead of inheriting an
open-ended exception. The gate now THROWS if fileLineAllowlist reappears in this file.
The gate was ALREADY RED at HEAD 290a4dcd9 before this change (17 violations, clean worktree): 11 files
had grown past 500 LOC or past an existing pin with no valid pin at all, and 5 root-barrel metrics were
over budget. Those were closed the same fails-closed way — a bytes-bound rootDebtPin / fileLineDebtPin —
and NOT by re-pinning any budget upward. Every budget number in this file is unchanged by RF-03; where a
pin sits above its budget the intended end-state is recorded in shrinkTarget/shrinkTargets on the pin
itself, so the ratchet target survives the temporary exemption. reviewBy for all RF-03 pins: 2026-11-16.
HOW TO EDIT A PINNED FILE (a debt pin does NOT make a file un-editable, and there is no bootstrapping
deadlock): make your source change, then in the SAME commit update that file's pin here — recompute
sourceSha256 over the new bytes, set the metric to the new measured value, set sourceCommit to the commit
you based on, and set a fresh reviewBy. sourceCommit is provenance only and is never resolved against the
object database (see validateDebtPin in scripts/check-barrel-budgets.mjs), precisely so that a re-pin does
not require a commit that does not exist yet. What the pin actually forbids is landing a change to a
capped file WITHOUT a reviewer looking at it. NOTE: packages/memory/src/index.ts and
packages/agent-adapters/src/index.ts carry BOTH a rootDebtPin and a fileLineDebtPins entry — editing
either one means refreshing both pins.

travel: shrinkTarget appeared exactly ONCE in the whole tree, inside an error-message template literal in
check-barrel-budgets.mjs, so it was never parsed, compared or enforced. Reconstructing every committed
version of this file shows what that cost: between 2026-08-04 and 2026-08-18 the numbers here moved UP 16

check-barrel-budgets.mjs now diffs this file against its committed base (default HEAD; --base-ref <ref> or
BARREL_BUDGET_BASE_REF, use the merge base in CI) and REJECTS any number that moved away from its target.
Since a target always sits below its pin, that means: DOWN is free, deleting a satisfied pin is free, UP
needs a signature. Every numeric leaf under packages is covered — budget caps, pin ceilings, aux budgets,
and shrinkTarget itself, so moving the goalpost is not a way around it.
acceptedGrowth              - array of signatures, each authorising ONE exact transition:
{ key, from, to, reason, approvedBy, date }. key is the slash-path of the
number under packages, e.g. @dzupagent/memory/rootDebtPin/maxRootIndexLines.
A record is consumed once (one signature cannot cover two raises), must not
be future-dated, and EXPIRES after 30 days so an old one cannot silently
re-authorise the same growth later. The failure message prints the exact
record to paste. Records are kept afterwards as an audit log.
acceptedGrowthApprovers     - OPTIONAL allowlist of who may sign. While it is absent, any non-empty
approvedBy is accepted and the gate prints a NOTE saying so. Add the list to
restrict signing authority; that is an owner decision, not an agent one.
shrinkTarget/shrinkTargets are no longer the source of truth for a target — the enforced budget is, and it
is always present (a pin only exists because the metric exceeded it). A declared copy is optional but must
EQUAL the budget; a softer third number fails the gate. In all 25 live pins it already did.
